With no `root_priority` field, priority defaults to `roots` list order:
listing `GROMACS` first here keeps `GROMACS 2025.0` (and `OpenMPI 4.1.6`),
yielding `LAMMPS 2023.08`. Reordering `roots` to `["LAMMPS", "GROMACS"]`
flips the outcome to `LAMMPS 2024.08` / `GROMACS 2024.4`. That coupling
(priority tied to incidental list order) is exactly what `root_priority`
lets you avoid.

# With root_priority: explicit and list-order-independent

```json
{
  "toolchain": {"name": "foss", "version": "2025b"},
  "roots": ["LAMMPS", "GROMACS"],
  "root_priority": ["GROMACS", "LAMMPS"],
  "pins": [],
  "forbid": [],
  "objective": "prefer_newer"
}
```

```bash
eb-stack stack solve \
  --easyconfigs fixtures/two_root_openmpi_conflict/easyconfigs \
  --stack-policy fixtures/two_root_openmpi_conflict/policies/priority_gromacs_roots_lammps_first.json \
  --lock-out /tmp/root-priority.lock.json --sbom-out /tmp/root-priority.cdx.json
# GROMACS 2025.0 (kept: prioritized)
# LAMMPS 2023.08 (yielded: not prioritized)
# OpenMPI 4.1.6 (forced by GROMACS's exact pin)
```

`roots` still lists `LAMMPS` first, but ~root_priority: ["GROMACS",
"LAMMPS"]` keeps `GROMACS~ at its newest version regardless. Swap the
`roots` order in the policy file and re-run: the outcome does not change,
because priority is now declared, not inferred.

# How the priority is applied

For each root in `root_priority` order (or `roots` order when
`root_priority` is omitted), `eb-stack` pins that root to the newest version
that is **still jointly feasible** with every higher-priority root already
pinned, then moves to the next root. Lower-priority roots yield whatever
version remains consistent once the higher-priority pins are fixed. A root
missing from an explicit `root_priority` list is appended in `roots` order,
so every root always participates.

# Next steps

- [Policy schema reference](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../reference/policy.html.md) for the exact
  `root_priority` field semantics.
- [[file:../explanation/optimization-model.org][Why this needs an optimization layer
  on top of SAT feasibility]].

# Which easyconfigs an easyblock change reaches

A change to an easyblock, generic or software-specific, or to a framework
module an easyblock imports, reaches the easyconfigs that use that class.
The class may be the `easyblock` line, the implied `EB_<Name>` class, a
subclass, an extension class, or a bundle component class.

# One changed file

`scripts/fetch-upstream-trees.sh` creates a checkout of the pinned trees and writes
`env.sh`. `EB_EASYBLOCKS` is easybuild-easyblocks v5.4.1.
`EB_EASYCONFIGS` is the develop easyconfigs directory.
`EB_EASYBUILD_FRAMEWORK` is easybuild-framework v5.4.1. Source `env.sh`
and pass those paths.

```bash
scripts/fetch-upstream-trees.sh
set -a
source "${EB_UPSTREAM_CACHE:-$HOME/.cache/eb-stack/upstream}/env.sh"
set +a
printf '%s\n' 'CMake/4.2.1-GCCcore-15.2.0' > /tmp/modules.txt

eb-stack easyblock-reach \
  --easyblocks "$EB_EASYBLOCKS" \
  --easyconfigs "$EB_EASYCONFIGS" \
  --file "$EB_EASYBLOCKS/easybuild/easyblocks/generic/cmakemake.py" \
  --installed /tmp/modules.txt \
  --reverse \
  --out-dir /tmp/cmakemake-reach
```

That command, against the trees `scripts/fetch-upstream-trees.sh` checked
out on 2026-10-24, printed:

```
easyconfigs=2352 installed=0 classes=39 reverse=5058 out=/tmp/cmakemake-reach
```

`installed` stays 0 when the modules file does not name a reached
module. The empty range `HEAD..HEAD` on that same checkout printed
`easyconfigs`0 installed`0 classes`0 reverse`0`.

`modules.txt` lists installed modules, one per line:
`name/version[-toolchain]versionsuffix`. Blank lines and `#` comments are
ignored.

The command writes `reach.toml`, `reach.json`, and `reach.md`. The TOML
file starts with the generated-file header. The markdown opens with the
same warning as an HTML comment. Neither is a file to merge.

# A commit range or a pull request

```bash
eb-stack easyblock-reach \
  --easyblocks "$EB_EASYBLOCKS" \
  --easyconfigs "$EB_EASYCONFIGS" \
  --range HEAD..HEAD \
  --out-dir /tmp/range-reach

eb-stack easyblock-reach \
  --easyblocks "$EB_EASYBLOCKS" \
  --framework "$EB_EASYBUILD_FRAMEWORK" \
  --easyconfigs "$EB_EASYCONFIGS" \
  --pr 4250 \
  --repo "$EB_EASYBLOCKS" \
  --base easybuild-easyblocks-v5.4.1 \
  --out-dir /tmp/pr4250-reach
```

`--range` is passed to `git diff --name-only`. `HEAD..HEAD` on the
pinned checkout changes no file. `--pr` fetches `refs/pull/N/head` and
diffs it against the merge-base with `--base` (default `develop`). The
pinned easyblocks checkout is the v5.4.1 tag, so pass
`--base easybuild-easyblocks-v5.4.1` when that is the tree `--repo`
has. `--repo` is the clone `git` reads; it defaults to the first
`--easyblocks` path. The class hierarchy is the working tree. A
deleted file is read from the base so its class is still seen.

# What counts as a use

- the `easyblock` line
- no `easyblock` line: `EB_<Name>` derived from the software name
- a subclass, read from the Python `class` statement, so `EB_GROMACS(CMakeMake)`
  is reached by a change to `CMakeMake`
- a nested class, so `EB_QuantumESPRESSOcmake(CMakeMake)` inside
  `EB_QuantumESPRESSO` reaches the QuantumESPRESSO easyconfigs
- a module-level alias bound to a class, so `Legacy = CMakeMake` is
  `CMakeMake`
- an extension's own `easyblock`, else `EB_<extname>` when that class
  exists, else `exts_classmap`, else `exts_defaultclass`
- a component's own `easyblock`, else `EB_<name>` when that class exists,
  else `default_easyblock`

A class that assigns `exts_defaultclass` overwrites the easyconfig.
`PythonBundle` assigns `PythonPackage`, including from inside `with`.
For a component, `default_easyblock` in the easyconfig wins over the
class.

A framework module reaches the easyblocks that import it, then their
subclasses. Imports inside `easybuild.framework` and `easybuild.tools`
are followed to the end of that graph. An easyblock that imports any
module on that path is reached. An easyblock that only imports another
easyblock is not, unless it subclasses a reached class.

`--reverse` lists modules that depend on a reached module and would need a
rebuild: runtime, builddependency, extension, or toolchain. Reached modules
are not listed again.

# Find shared builds across open pull requests

Goal: for every open pull request that changes an easystack, write what it
would build on the current stack, and which of those modules more than one
open pull request would build.

The inputs are the pull requests' easystack files, the release easyconfigs,
and a list of installed modules. Nothing from a pull request is executed.

# Run it on the recorded pull requests

`tests/pr_overlap_layer/` records pull requests 1585 and 1728 from
European Environment for Scientific Software Installations (EESSI) software-layer `b2c10c7278f8b741f4053ddb2907dc4d062063d1`. Both
change
`easystacks/software.eessi.io/2026.06/eessi-2026.06-eb-5.4.0-2026.1.yml`.
1585 adds `SciPy-bundle-2026.05-gfbf-2026.1.eb`. 1728 adds
`PLUMED-2.10.0-foss-2026.1.eb`, and that recipe depends on SciPy-bundle
2026.05. The easyconfigs are the 109 modules the two closures reach,
copied from easybuild-easyconfigs develop
`981d2123dddccca9ce0b15f9eb2643e872332f5e`. `installed.txt` is a comment,
because this checkout has no mounted prefix.

The 1585/1728 pair is a replay of a recorded state. Pull request 1585
merged on 2026-09-04. The recorded base of 1728 already lists
`SciPy-bundle-2026.05-gfbf-2026.1.eb`. The two used different bases.
The command replays 1728's easystack against an empty `installed.txt`,
which is why the pair shares 91 modules. To run the same command on
live pull requests, clone `EESSI/software-layer`, write one JSON file
per open pull request with `examples/eessi-pr-overlap/fetch-prs.sh`,
and pass the prefix's installed module list. The next section is that
run.

```bash
eb-stack pr-overlap --pr tests/pr_overlap_layer/prs.json \
  --easyconfigs tests/pr_overlap_layer \
  --installed tests/pr_overlap_layer/installed.txt \
  --installed-label none \
  --generated-at 2026-10-24T00:00:00Z \
  --repo-url https://github.com/EESSI/software-layer \
  --eessi-version 2026.06 \
  --merge-order \
  --out-dir /tmp/pr-overlap-out
```

The command prints `prs`2 records`2 shared_modules`91 skipped_easyconfigs`0`.
`--merge-order` writes `/tmp/pr-overlap-out/merge-order.toml`. Position 1
is pull request 1585, which builds the 91 modules. Position 2 is pull
request 1728, which builds the remaining 18 once 1585 is first, and
`after` is 1585.

`fetch-prs.sh` lives in this repository at
`examples/eessi-pr-overlap/fetch-prs.sh`. It writes one JSON file per open
pull request from a clone. Pass those files as repeated `--pr` arguments,
and pass `--commit-tree NAME`DIR` and `--easyblocks-commit NAME`DIR` for
each directory it wrote. `--easyconfigs` is the easyconfigs tree that comes
with the EasyBuild version the easystack names. `--installed-modulerc`
is that prefix's `modules/all`. `--filter-deps` drops dependencies the
way EasyBuild does; when the flag is omitted and `EASYBUILD_FILTER_DEPS`
is set, the command reads the variable.

For a `from-commit` pin, `--commit-tree` is the whole easyconfigs tree at
that commit. `--easyblocks` is the EasyBuild release's
`easybuild/easyblocks` package. `--easyblocks-commit` is the files one
`include-easyblocks-from-commit` touches.

For another architecture, pass that architecture's installed list and
`--include-path` for its substring. Do not also exclude the same
substring. `--installed-label` is the string recorded on the report.

# Run it on a mounted stack

From a clone of `EESSI/software-layer`, with `gh` authenticated for public
reads. `EB_EASYCONFIGS` and `EB_EASYBLOCKS` come from
`scripts/fetch-upstream-trees.sh`. `examples/eessi-pr-overlap/fetch-prs.sh`
writes one JSON file per open pull request. The outputs go under `/tmp`
so the checkout stays unchanged.

```bash
scripts/fetch-upstream-trees.sh
set -a
source "${EB_UPSTREAM_CACHE:-$HOME/.cache/eb-stack/upstream}/env.sh"
set +a
examples/eessi-pr-overlap/fetch-prs.sh EESSI/software-layer 2026.06 /tmp/pr-overlap-in/
find "$EESSI_SOFTWARE_PATH/software" -mindepth 2 -maxdepth 2 -type d -printf '%P\n' \
  | sort > /tmp/pr-overlap-installed.txt
eb-stack pr-overlap --pr /tmp/pr-overlap-in/prs/*.json \
  $(for d in /tmp/pr-overlap-in/commit-trees/*/; do printf -- '--commit-tree %s=%s ' "$(basename "$d")" "$d"; done) \
  $(for d in /tmp/pr-overlap-in/easyblocks/*/; do printf -- '--easyblocks-commit %s=%s ' "$(basename "$d")" "$d"; done) \
  --easyconfigs "$EB_EASYCONFIGS" \
  --easyblocks "$EB_EASYBLOCKS" \
  --installed /tmp/pr-overlap-installed.txt \
  --installed-modulerc "$EESSI_SOFTWARE_PATH/modules/all" \
  --filter-deps "$EASYBUILD_FILTER_DEPS" \
  --installed-label x86_64/amd/zen4 \
  --generated-at 2026-10-22T00:00:00Z \
  --out-dir /tmp/pr-overlap-out
```

# Read which modules are shared

`/tmp/pr-overlap-out/prs/<N>.toml` lists `to_build` as one sorted line per
module. Duplicates across those lines are the overlap:

```bash
awk '/^to_build = \[\]/{next} /^to_build = \[/{f=1; next} f && /^\]/{f=0; next} f' /tmp/pr-overlap-out/prs/*.toml | sort | uniq -d
```

On the recorded pair, that list has 91 modules.
`/tmp/pr-overlap-out/overlap.md` is the same answer as a table. The
SciPy-bundle row names pull requests 1585 and 1728.
`/tmp/pr-overlap-out/overlap.toml`
is the index. Closed pull requests have no file: each run rewrites `prs/`
to the open set.

# Wire it into CI

The draft workflow is
`examples/eessi-pr-overlap/pr_dependency_overlap.yml`. It is not installed
in `EESSI/software-layer` from this repository.

On the software-layer repository:

1. Exempt `gh_action_pr_dependency_overlap` from the branch push restriction,
   the same way `gh_action_update_software_layer_commit_sha` is exempt, so
   `github-actions[bot]` can push to that one branch. `main` stays protected.
2. Copy `pr_dependency_overlap.yml` to `.github/workflows/` and
   `fetch-prs.sh` to `.github/workflows/scripts/fetch_pr_easystacks.sh`.
3. Set `EB_STACK_VERSION` and `EB_STACK_SHA256` in the workflow to a release
   that carries `pr-overlap`.

The workflow runs on a schedule and on `workflow_dispatch`, from `main`. It
mounts the stack, writes the three output files, and pushes them to
`gh_action_pr_dependency_overlap` without force. It opens no pull request
and posts no comment. The publish job commits only when a build set changed.
A timestamp change alone is not committed.

The compute step loads `EESSI-extend` and passes `$EASYBUILD_FILTER_DEPS`,
`--installed-modulerc`, `--easyblocks`, and one `--easyblocks-commit` per
directory `fetch-prs.sh` wrote. The filter list is not written into the
workflow file.

Why the files are regenerated on every run, and why a second build of a
shared module overwrites the first binary, is covered in
[from one easystack line to a build set](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../explanation/pr-overlap.html.md).

# Order the merges

`--merge-order` writes `/tmp/pr-overlap-out/merge-order.toml` and appends a
table to `/tmp/pr-overlap-out/overlap.md`. The command is the one in
[[*Run it on the recorded pull requests][Run it on the recorded pull requests]].
Position 1 is 1585 (91 modules). Position 2 is 1728 (18 modules), and
`after` is 1585. The rule is in
[Merge order and knock-on](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../explanation/pr-overlap.html.md).

# What one merge changes

`--impact N` writes `/tmp/pr-overlap-out/merge-impact.toml` and does not
write `merge-order.toml`. It is the effect of merging N on its own, not
the residual after earlier steps of `--merge-order`. A number that is not
in the input exits with `--impact N: no pull request with that number`.
A pull request that is in the input but changes nothing exits with
`--impact N: pull request N has no record (no easyconfigs or easystack change)`.
The recorded command above does not pass `--impact`.

# For easybuild-easyconfigs pull requests

The recorded open pull requests are `tests/pr_overlap_easyconfigs_open/`,
read on 2026-10-24 and closed against develop
`981d2123dddccca9ce0b15f9eb2643e872332f5e`.

```bash
eb-stack pr-overlap \
  --kind easyconfigs \
  --pr tests/pr_overlap_easyconfigs_open/prs.json \
  --easyconfigs tests/pr_overlap_easyconfigs_open/tree \
  --generated-at 2026-10-24T00:00:00Z \
  --repo-url https://github.com/easybuilders/easybuild-easyconfigs \
  --out-dir /tmp/ec-open-out
```

The command prints `prs`4 records`4 shared_modules`1 skipped_easyconfigs`0`.
The files under `/tmp/ec-open-out` match
`tests/pr_overlap_easyconfigs_open/expected/`.

`--installed` is omitted, so `to_build` equals `new_modules`. `--repo-url`
links each pull request number in `overlap.md`. 22823 and 24575 share
`Mathematica/14.2.1`.

`eb-stack pr-overlap --kind easyconfigs --open OWNER/NAME` is the command
that reads those pull requests. It calls `fetch_open_easyconfig_prs`.
`examples/easyconfigs-pr-overlap/fetch-prs.sh` collects the same JSON with
`gh` and git, from a clone, and does not check a pull request out. The
page
[close open easybuild-easyconfigs pull requests](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/easyconfigs-pr-overlap.html.md)
says which of the two is the one the tool calls.

# Close open easybuild-easyconfigs pull requests

Goal: for each open pull request on easybuild-easyconfigs, name the
easyconfigs it adds or changes, the dependency closure of those files
against a pinned develop tree, and the modules it shares with the other
open pull requests.

The file text is data. Nothing from a pull request is executed, and
nothing is posted back to the pull request.

# Recorded open pull requests

On 2026-10-24 the public GitHub API had these four open pull requests.
develop was `981d2123dddccca9ce0b15f9eb2643e872332f5e`.

| Number | Head | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 22823 | `251770fd65` | added `Mathematica-14.2.1.eb` |
| 24575 | `26cbff81cb` | added the same path |
| 27131 | `dc56db8eae` | added `aria2-1.37.0-GCCcore-15.2.0.eb` |
| 27215 | `6993418f56` | added `nghttp3-1.13.1-GCCcore-13.2.0.eb` and modified three nghttp3 files |

`tests/pr_overlap_easyconfigs_open.rs` runs:

```bash
eb-stack pr-overlap --kind easyconfigs \
  --pr tests/pr_overlap_easyconfigs_open/prs.json \
  --easyconfigs tests/pr_overlap_easyconfigs_open/tree \
  --generated-at 2026-10-24T00:00:00Z \
  --repo-url https://github.com/easybuilders/easybuild-easyconfigs \
  --out-dir /tmp/ec-open-out
```

The command printed `prs`4 records`4 shared_modules`1 skipped_easyconfigs`0`
and exited 0. `--installed` is omitted, so `to_build` is `new_modules`.

22823 and 24575 both add
`easybuild/easyconfigs/m/Mathematica/Mathematica-14.2.1.eb`. The module is
`Mathematica/14.2.1`. `overlap.toml` records three rows for that pair:
`same-file`, `same-module`, and `shared-new-module`. The file is not on
that develop commit, so each closure is the one new module.

27131 adds `aria2/1.37.0-GCCcore-15.2.0`. The closure has 53 modules and
one of them is new. Nothing is unresolved.

27215 changes four nghttp3 easyconfigs. The closure has 152 modules. The
new module is `nghttp3/1.13.1-GCCcore-13.2.0`. The record says
`nghttp3/1.13.1-GCCcore-13.2.0 needs CUnit ==2.1-3`. Reverse dependents
include LibSoup, WebKitGTK+, nghttp2, ngtcp2, and
`wxPython/4.2.5-gfbf-2025a`.

The checked-in tree is those closure modules plus `gfbf-2025a.eb`.
wxPython is built with gfbf 2025a, and that definition pins GCC 14.2.0,
which is how LibSoup at GCC 14.2.0 stays on the reverse-dependency walk.
The bytes under `tests/pr_overlap_easyconfigs_open/expected/` are the same
bytes this command wrote against the full develop tree. The `.eb` files
are a subset of easybuild-easyconfigs (GPL-2.0); the license text is
`tests/pr_overlap_easyconfigs_open/EASYCONFIGS-GPLv2.txt`.

# Read the pull requests over HTTPS

`fetch_open_easyconfig_prs` GETs
`https://api.github.com/repos/<owner>/<name>/pulls?state=open` and, for
each pull request, the changed-file list. Head text is
`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<owner>/<name>/<sha>/<path>`. Base
text is the same URL with the base ref (`develop` unless another ref is
set). A 404 on the base means the file was added. No token is sent.

The command the tool runs is `eb-stack pr-overlap --kind easyconfigs --open OWNER/NAME`.
It calls `fetch_open_easyconfig_prs` and writes the
same records as `--pr`. `--base-ref` is the base ref in the raw URL
(`develop` when the flag is omitted). The ignored test
`live_github_open_easyconfigs_pull_request` calls the same function
against `easybuilders/easybuild-easyconfigs`, one list page, one pull
request, and one easyconfig file.

`examples/easyconfigs-pr-overlap/fetch-prs.sh` is the clone-side collector.
It uses `gh` and git to write the same JSON, and it does not check a pull
request out. Use it when the inputs already come from a local clone. Use
`--open` when the command should fetch the pull requests itself.

# Easyconfigs merge order

`--merge-order` and `--impact` answer a different question: in which
order to merge open pull requests, and which other build sets one merge
changes. For an easyconfigs run the edges are the `depends-on` rows in
`overlap.toml` from the same run. `after` lists the pull request that
adds the module, and `resolves` lists those modules. The software-layer
run is
[find shared builds across open pull requests](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/pr-overlap.html.md).

# What an in-place patch forces EESSI to rebuild

Goal: the patched easyconfigs keep their filenames and versions. Report
which installed modules must be rebuilt, which need a review, and which
link the patched package as a shared library. The set is the rebuild
closure: every installed module that depends on the patched one within
its toolchain generation, and no module from another generation.

# Run it on the fixture

```bash
eb-stack rebuild-set \
  --changed tests/rebuild_set_fixtures/changed.txt \
  --easystack tests/rebuild_set_fixtures/eessi-2026.06-eb-5.4.0-2026.1.yml \
  --easystack tests/rebuild_set_fixtures/20261001-eb-5.4.1-zlib.yml \
  --easyconfigs tests/rebuild_set_fixtures/release \
  --easyblocks tests/rebuild_set_fixtures/easyblocks \
  --installed tests/rebuild_set_fixtures/installed.txt \
  --installed-modulerc tests/rebuild_set_fixtures/modules/all \
  --installed-label x86_64/amd/zen4 \
  --generated-at 2026-10-22T12:00:00Z \
  --out-dir /tmp/rebuild-out
```

The command prints:

```
changed=2 rows=8 must-rebuild=2 review=2 no-rebuild=4 missing=1 easystacks=2 skipped_easyconfigs=0 out=/tmp/rebuild-out
```

# Run it on a mounted stack

From a clone of `EESSI/software-layer`, with the 2026.06 stack mounted.
`EB_EASYCONFIGS` and `EB_EASYBLOCKS` come from
`scripts/fetch-upstream-trees.sh`:

```bash
scripts/fetch-upstream-trees.sh
set -a
source "${EB_UPSTREAM_CACHE:-$HOME/.cache/eb-stack/upstream}/env.sh"
set +a
eb-stack rebuild-set \
  --changed changed.txt \
  --easystack easystacks/software.eessi.io/2026.06/*.yml \
  --easystack easystacks/software.eessi.io/2026.06/rebuilds/*.yml \
  $(for d in commit-trees/*/; do printf -- '--commit-tree %s=%s ' "$(basename "$d")" "$d"; done) \
  --easyconfigs "$EB_EASYCONFIGS" \
  --easyblocks "$EB_EASYBLOCKS" \
  --installed installed.txt \
  --installed-modulerc "$EESSI_SOFTWARE_PATH/modules/all" \
  --filter-deps "$EASYBUILD_FILTER_DEPS" \
  --installed-label x86_64/amd/zen4 \
  --generated-at 2026-10-22T12:00:00Z \
  --out-dir /tmp/rebuild-out
```

`--commit-tree NAME=DIR` resolves a `from-commit` pin, the same way as
`pr-overlap`. `--filter-deps` drops dependency tuples before the walk.
When the flag is omitted and `EASYBUILD_FILTER_DEPS` is set, the command
reads the variable. `--prefix` is an install prefix: for each patched
module the command reads `software/<name>/<version>/lib**/**.a` there.
`--check-static` needs `--prefix`.

`--changed` is an easyconfig filename, repeated, or a file that is not an
`.eb`: one filename per line, blank lines and `#` comments skipped.
`--easystack` is each deployed easystack. A `from-commit` pin is resolved
with `--commit-tree`, the same way as `pr-overlap`. Pass the CPU
easystacks for the target you are asking about, and leave out `accel/`
and `additional_arch/` unless that is the stack you mounted.

`--easyconfigs` is the easyconfigs tree of the EasyBuild release the
stack uses. `--filter-deps` drops dependency tuples before the walk, with
the same matching as `pr-overlap`. It does not remove an extension from a
bundle's `exts_list`. When the flag is omitted and `EASYBUILD_FILTER_DEPS`
is set, the command reads the variable. `--installed-modulerc` is that
prefix's `modules/all`. `--easyblocks` is the EasyBuild release's
`easybuild/easyblocks` package. A missing class is recorded. The module
stays in the set, because it is already installed.

# Read the three files

`out/rebuild-set.md` is the table: changed easyconfig, dependent, edge
kind, class, and reason, then the counts. A changed filename that is not
in the deployed graph is listed and has no row. `out/rebuild-set.json` is
the same document.

`out/rebuilds/<YYYYMMDD>-eb-<version>-cve-patches.yml` lists class
must-rebuild only, with `rebuild: true`. The date is taken from
`--generated-at` (or from the current date in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC)). One file per EasyBuild
version named by the easystack filenames. A second run replaces the
`rebuilds/*.yml` files from the previous run.

`--prefix` is `$EESSI_SOFTWARE_PATH`. For each patched module the command
reads `software/<name>/<version>/lib**/**.a`. A patched module with
no static archive cannot have been linked statically, so a
builddependency-only dependent is no-rebuild and the reason is ~no static
archive installed~. Archives that are installed keep the row in review
and are named. A missing install directory is a note, and the row stays
in review. A prefix with no `software` directory is an error.

A review dependent is one row. The changed column lists every patched
easyconfig that put it there.

`--check-static` needs `--prefix`. For each remaining review dependent it
reads defined dynamic symbols, the names `nm -D --defined-only` prints,
from the installed Executable and Linkable Format (ELF) files. The patched library's names come from its
shared objects, or from the archive members when the install has no
shared object. A hit is must-rebuild. No hit is no-rebuild. An empty export set
stays in review, because there was nothing to look for.

The symbol scan can go wrong. It sees dynamic symbols only, so a hidden,
local, or inlined static link is a false no-rebuild. A short name shared
with another library is a false must-rebuild. Scripts, bytecode, and
libraries opened with dlopen are invisible. A static archive shows that a
static link was possible, not that it happened.

Why a runtime dependency needs no rebuild, and why a bundle extension
does, is covered in
[what an in-place patch forces a rebuild of](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../explanation/rebuild-set.html.md).

# Which modules carry a component, and what that forces rebuilt

Goal: a Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) record names a component and a version. List every easyconfig and
installed module in one toolchain generation that carries it, then feed
the recipes that contain it into the rebuild closure.

# Run it

The recorded slice in this checkout is enough to see the counts. The
files are copies of easybuild-easyconfigs develop
`981d2123dddccca9ce0b15f9eb2643e872332f5e`, the pin in
`scripts/fetch-upstream-trees.sh`, and the upstream `LICENSE` is in
that directory.

```bash
eb-stack component-reach \
  --component curl \
  --version '>=8,<9' \
  --generation 2026.1 \
  --easyconfigs tests/component_reach_recorded \
  --out-dir /tmp/component-reach
```

The command prints:

```
component=curl version=>=8,<9 generation=2026.1 carriers=2 changed=1 must-rebuild=1 review=0 no-rebuild=1 out=/tmp/component-reach
```

cURL 8.17.0 is the module. git 2.52.0 depends on that cURL and is the
no-rebuild row. The same command against the pinned easyconfigs tree
and a deployed easystack uses `scripts/fetch-upstream-trees.sh`. Pass
one of `--component`, `--purl`, or `--cve`.

```bash
scripts/fetch-upstream-trees.sh
set -a
source "${EB_UPSTREAM_CACHE:-$HOME/.cache/eb-stack/upstream}/env.sh"
set +a
eb-stack component-reach \
  --component curl \
  --version '>=8,<9' \
  --generation 2026.1 \
  --easyconfigs "$EB_EASYCONFIGS" \
  --easystack "$EB_EESSI_SOFTWARE_LAYER/easystacks/software.eessi.io/2026.06/eessi-2026.06-eb-5.4.0-2026.1.yml" \
  --out-dir /tmp/component-reach-full
```

The command prints:

```
component=curl version=>=8,<9 generation=2026.1 carriers=23 changed=2 must-rebuild=1 review=106 no-rebuild=16 out=/tmp/component-reach-full
```

The changed files are `cURL-8.17.0-GCCcore-15.2.0.eb` and
`cargo-c-0.10.23-GCCcore-15.2.0.eb`. The must-rebuild row is
`cURL/8.17.0-GCCcore-15.2.0`, reason `patched easyconfig`.

`--easystack` and `--installed` narrow the walk to a deployed prefix.
`--filter-deps` drops dependency tuples before the closure walk. When
that flag is omitted and `EASYBUILD_FILTER_DEPS` is set, the command
reads the variable. The recorded command above passes neither, so every
easyconfig in the generation is the stack.

`--component` is the name. Matching ignores ASCII letter case, so `curl` matches
`cURL` and `jupyterlab` matches `JupyterLab`. The match is a whole token,
so `jupyterlab` does not match `jupyterlab-server` and `curl` does not
match `libcurl`.

`--version` is an exact version, `*` for any version, or a requirement
such as `>=8,<9`. It is required with `--component`. With `--purl` it
replaces the version in the URL. `--cve` does not take `--version`: the
versions come from Open Source Vulnerabilities (OSV).

`--purl` is a package URL, for example
`pkg:cargo/rustls-webpki@0.102.8` or `pkg:pypi/urllib3@2.5.0`. The type
selects which carriers count. `generic` and `github` match the
easyconfig name: the module, a dependency, a builddependency, a
component, a source, or a patch. `pypi`, `cargo`, `npm`, `golang`, and
`cran` match an extension or a bundled component of that language.
`cargo` also matches a crate, and `pypi` also matches a wheel. Any
other type is rejected: the command exits 2 and the error says that
purl type has no carrier model. `pkg:cargo/curl` and `pkg:npm/curl` do
not match the cURL easyconfig. `--component curl` still matches that
recipe by name. A version in the URL is the requirement unless
`--version` is also passed.

`--cve` is a CVE id or another OSV id. The record is fetched from
`https://api.osv.dev/v1/vulns/<id>`. A CVE record often has only a git
range and no package. Advisory aliases (`GHSA-`, `RUSTSEC-`, `PYSEC-`,
`GO-`) are followed, up to eight. Named tags such as `libXpm-3.5.17`
become exact versions. Git tags such as `XORG-6_8_0` do not. Each
affected package is searched on its own, and a version matches when any
of that package's requirements match or when it is one of the exact
versions. A range whose type is not SEMVER or ECOSYSTEM, and an event
that does not parse as a version requirement, is listed under
Unresolved ranges in the markdown. It is not discarded. When every
range on a package was unparsed, that package counts as review and its
carrier list stays empty. The three output files are then one document
with `kind` set to `cve`, and `results` contains one reach document per
package. The summary line includes the closure counts `changed`,
`must-rebuild`, `review`, and `no-rebuild`.

`--generation` is the toolchain generation, for example `2026.1` or
`2025a`. A recipe is in that generation when its toolchain version is
that string, or when its toolchain is a member of the known foss
hierarchy for that generation. `GCCcore-15.2.0` and `GCC-15.2.0` belong
to `2026.1`. `GCCcore-14.2.0` belongs to `2025a`, `GCCcore-14.3.0` to
`2025b`, and `GCCcore-13.3.0` to `2024a`. A system toolchain does not. A
module built with another generation is not a row.

`--easystack-url` repeats. The URL must be `https://`. The body is an
easystack, read the same way as `--easystack`. Local files and URLs are
one stack.

# What carries it

- the easyconfig's own module name and version;
- a `dependencies` or `builddependencies` tuple;
- a bundle `components` entry;
- a Python, R, or Perl extension in `exts_list`;
- a Cargo crate, from a `crates` tuple or from a filename such as
  `libz-sys-1.1.29.tar.gz`, including a vendored `+name-version` fragment
  such as `0.4.89+curl-8.20.0`. A Cargo recipe also matches a crate that
  appears only as a checksum key, such as `rustls-webpki-0.102.8.tar.gz`.
  The recipe's own tarball is not that crate;
- a Python wheel: a `.whl` filename in `sources` or `checksums`, an
  `exts_list` entry whose source is a wheel (`pastel`), or a top-level
  `source_tmpl` that names a wheel (`cleo`). The role is `wheel`;
- a vendored or bundled filename in `sources` or `patches` whose name
  contains the component and a version;
- a line in `--compat-layer`, `name version` or `name==version`, `#`
  comments skipped.

A dependency or a builddependency lists the recipe as a carrier and does
not add it to the patched set. The component's own module is the root,
and those recipes are its closure. A module, bundle component, extension,
crate, source, or patch means the recipe contains the bytes, and that
filename is a patched root.

The compat layer is not an easyconfig. Pass it with `--compat-layer`. A
hit is a row with an empty easyconfig and a note that it has no rebuild
edge.

`--filter-deps` drops dependency tuples before the closure walk, the same
way as `rebuild-set`, and does not strip `exts_list`. When the flag is
omitted and `EASYBUILD_FILTER_DEPS` is set, the command reads it.

# The closure

With no `--easystack`, every easyconfig in the generation is the stack.
With no `--installed`, every module in the generation is treated as
installed, so the reverse walk does not stop. Pass both when the question
is a mounted prefix: then only those modules are visited.

The closure is the rebuild set of the containing recipes, inside the
generation. Classes are the same as `rebuild-set`: `must-rebuild`,
`review`, and `no-rebuild`. This command does not read a prefix or scan
static symbols.

# Read the three files

`out/component-reach.md` is the carrier table and the closure table.
`out/component-reach.json` is the same document.
`out/component-reach.toml` starts with
`# Generated by `eb-stack component-reach`.`
Schema version 1. See [output formats](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../reference/formats.html.md).

# From-commit pins already in an EasyBuild release

An easystack `from-commit` pin asks EasyBuild to take an easyconfig from
that commit of easybuild-easyconfigs. Pin it when the file is newer than
the EasyBuild release the stack builds with. A pin whose commit is already
in that release does nothing. Removing it is safe only when the easyconfig
at the pin is the same blob as at the release tag. A later edit, such as
the glibc 2.43 patch on UCX 1.18.0 and 1.19.0, means the release file is
not the pinned file, and a person has to decide.

# Check the easystacks

`--easybuild-version 5.4.0` names the release. When the flag is omitted,
the command reads `eb-X.Y.Z` from the file name
(`20261011-eb-5.4.0-UCX.yml`). The flag overrides the file name. With
neither, the command exits 2 and names `--easybuild-version`.

```bash
eb-stack stack from-commit \
  --easystack 20261011-eb-5.4.0-UCX.yml \
  --easyconfigs-repo "$EB_EASYCONFIGS" \
  --easyblocks-repo "$EB_EASYBLOCKS"
```

`--easyconfigs-repo` is an easybuild-easyconfigs checkout, tags included.
`--easyblocks-repo` is the easybuild-easyblocks checkout, and it is required
only when an entry sets `include-easyblocks-from-commit`. The tags are
`easybuild-easyconfigs-vX.Y.Z` and `easybuild-easyblocks-vX.Y.Z`.

Each pin is one line:

```
status=released blob=differs version=5.4.0 tag=easybuild-easyconfigs-v5.4.0 kind=from-commit commit=d438adc file=UCX-1.18.0-GCCcore-14.2.0.eb easystack=20261011-eb-5.4.0-UCX.yml
pins=1 released=1 newer=0 unknown=0
```

`released` means `git merge-base --is-ancestor` says the commit is in the
tag. `newer` means the commit is in the checkout and is not in the tag.
`unknown` means the commit or the tag is missing. The command does not
guess which. `reason`commit-missing` or `reason`tag-missing` says which
one.

For a `released` `from-commit` pin, `blob` compares the easyconfig blob in
the tree at the pin with the blob at the tag. `same` means one object.
`differs` means the path is missing on one side, the hashes differ, or
more than one path has that filename. `released` and `same` can be
removed. `released` and `differs` needs a person.

An `include-easyblocks-from-commit` pin has no single easyconfig in that
repository. `blob` there compares the tree of the pin with the tree of
`easybuild-easyblocks-vX.Y.Z`. `same` means the release tree is the pinned
tree.

The command exits 0 when no pin is `released`. It exits 1 when any pin is
`released`, including a pin whose blob is `same`. `--json` prints the same
fields as JSON. `eb_stack_from_commit` returns that report.

# Command-line reference

`eb-stack` has six namespaced command groups (`package`, `recipe`,
`stack`, `target`, `campaign`, `repro`), four reports (`easyblock-reach`,
`pr-overlap`, `rebuild-set`, `component-reach`), and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server.
`--version` prints the crate version. All paths written by package commands
are deterministic bundle artifacts.

# Exit status

| Code | When |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | The command finished the work it was asked to do |
| 1 | The work was attempted and failed: a missing or unreadable file, a document that does not parse, a check that found errors, a network fetch that failed, a doctor probe, or a campaign whose build failed |
| 2 | The command line was rejected before that work: a missing or unknown flag (clap), or a flag value or combination the command does not accept |

A rejected value names the flag and the value. A missing file names the flag and the path. Status 2 is the same status clap already uses. A recipe that fails `recipe lint` or `recipe check` is status 1: the files were read and the check failed. `stack from-commit` is status 1 when any pin is `released`, and status 0 when every pin is `newer` or `unknown` or the files name no pin. A file name with no `eb-X.Y.Z`, and no `--easybuild-version`, is status 2.

`--help` for every command has an example and a description of every flag. A default that the command applies is printed in that help. A directory that receives several artifacts is `--out-dir`. A single output file is `--out` (`--lock-out` for the lock `stack solve` writes). `--installed`, `--easyconfigs`, `--filter-deps`, and `--generated-at` use those names on every command that takes them.

Package commands take the toolchain as `--toolchain name/version`, the spelling `stack solve` uses. `--toolchain system`, `--toolchain SYSTEM`, and `--toolchain system/` select the SYSTEM toolchain. Its version is empty. `package inspect` and `package plan` accept a lone `--toolchain-version` and use `foss`. `package bump` does not.

# Command map

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `package inspect` | Parse conda-forge, Spack, PyPI, Comprehensive R Archive Network (CRAN), Cargo, LuaRocks, or Raku into a manifest and planned software bill of materials (SBOM) |
| `package plan` | Materialize profiles, solve with Resolvo, and emit recipes |
| `package bump` | Retarget an EasyBuild recipe and write the same canonical bundle |
| `recipe easyblock` | Print the easyblock class name EasyBuild derives for a software name |
| `recipe templates` | Emit template constants and derived-key rules, or the values `--name` and `--version` resolve |
| `recipe hierarchy` | Emit known toolchain hierarchies as JSON |
| `recipe check` | Validate metadata and robot dependency availability |
| `recipe lint` / `recipe format` | Report upstream CI, test-suite, and review findings (E999, F541, W605, W291, E501, E2xx, `EB_*`; `eb --check-contrib` merged when `eb` is installed) or mechanically wrap E501 lines |
| `stack solve` / `stack sbom` | Solve a multi-root stack or emit SBOM from a lock |
| `stack order` | Sequence every pinned build a set of roots needs |
| `stack easystack` | Write a lock as the YAML `eb --easystack` reads |
| `stack sections` | Regroup a Jenkins build list under a previous list's headers |
| `stack from-commit` | Report `from-commit` pins already contained in an EasyBuild release |
| `repro summary` | Print a reproduction scoreboard from collected case scores |
| `pr-overlap` | Close open pull-request easystack additions against an installed stack and report shared builds |
| `rebuild-set` | Classify the installed reverse dependents of easyconfigs patched in place |
| `component-reach` | List who carries a component in one generation and close their rebuild set |
| `target list` / `target doctor` | Resolve layered target configuration and probe it |
| `campaign run` / `campaign status` | Execute or inspect a persisted build campaign |
| `campaign finding ...` | Claim and resolve typed build findings |
| `mcp [--workspace]` | Serve each CLI workflow over stdio, including `pr-overlap`, `rebuild-set`, `component-reach`, and `easyblock-reach`, with recipe file tools rooted at `--workspace` |
| `easyblock-reach` | Report easyconfigs and installed modules reached by an easyblock or framework change |

# Package commands

## `package inspect`

```bash
eb-stack package inspect \
  --source PATH \
  --format auto|conda-forge|spack|pypi|cran|cargo|luarocks|raku \
  --toolchain foss/2026.1 \
  [--package-config PACKAGE.toml]... \
  --out-dir BUNDLE
```

This writes `package.plan.json` and `package.sbom.cdx.json`. It does not solve
profiles or emit recipes, so it establishes no claim-ladder rung.

## `package plan`

```bash
eb-stack package plan \
  --source PATH \
  --format auto|conda-forge|spack|pypi|cran|cargo|luarocks|raku \
  --toolchain foss/2026.1 \
  [--package-config PACKAGE.toml]... \
  [--source-checksum DIGEST]... \
  [--package-index FILE] \
  --easyconfigs UPSTREAM \
  [--easyconfigs OVERLAY]... \
  --stack-policy STACK.toml \
  [--package-catalog CATALOG.toml]... \
  [--package-sources SOURCES.toml]... \
  [--easybuild-source DIR]... \
  [--conda-source DIR]... \
  [--spack-source DIR]... \
  [--cargo-source DIR]... \
  --out-dir BUNDLE
```

Package configs apply in argument order; later metadata, build policy, aliases,
and profile values override earlier layers. Later robot paths override earlier paths for the same EasyBuild identity.
`build.patches` replaces the existing patch list by default. Set
`patches_mode = "merge"` in the layer's `[build]` table to retain foreign or
preceding patches while adding or refining artifacts by filename.
Each requested product profile is solved independently and emits one lock plus
one conventional `.eb` file. The default profile has no suffix; non-default
profiles use their declared `versionsuffix`.

Every emitted source needs a SHA-256 checksum. When a foreign recipe provides
only a version control system (VCS) commit, repeat `--source-checksum` once for every source artifact in
manifest order. The values replace the positional source checksums in both the
manifest/SBOM and every emitted recipe. Planning fails before emission when
the count, shape, or completeness is invalid.

`--package-index FILE` supplies a version for a dependency that states none.
The file is either a CRAN `PACKAGES` index or a `name==version` list, one pin
per line. A range is not a version and supplies nothing.

Passing `--easyconfigs` always uses the closure writer, because that tree is
also a discovery root. The bundle then contains `closure.plan.json`,
`closure.sbom.cdx.json`, and `build-order.json` even when no companion was
needed. `--emit-easyblock` does not combine with that writer.

When a direct dependency has no compatible robot candidate, further closure
inputs close the hole without inventing versions:

- `--package-sources` layers ordered EasyBuild / conda-forge / Spack / Cargo roots;
- `--easybuild-source`, `--conda-source`, `--spack-source`, and `--cargo-source` push roots
  without a TOML file (order is discovery order);
- `--package-catalog` layers explicit foreign or `easybuild-bump` providers as
  ordered overrides.
- `--emit-easyblock` renders an easyblock skeleton for the package into
  `easyblocks/<letter>/<module>.py`, writes it next to the recipes, names the
  derived class as the easyblock and moves the variant options out of the
  emitted recipes. Without it a package that owes an easyblock gets a
  `missing-easyblock` residual. It does not combine with closure planning.
  `package bump` takes the same flag.

Robot candidates win over catalog entries. A closed plan writes companion
packages under `packages/`, a shared `easyconfigs/` overlay, topological
`build-order.json`, and `closure.sbom.cdx.json`. See
[package bundles](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/package-bundles.html.md) and the new-package how-to.

`--format cargo` reads `Cargo.toml` or crates.io JSON. A `Cargo.toml` names
no crate tarball, so plan stops with ~foreign package plan has no source
artifacts~. The crates.io JSON carries the checksum, and that is what plan
emits from. A PyPI leftover
whose run dependency is a PyO3 crate is closed by `--cargo-source`, not
by a pip extra. Extra site packages that Warehouse omits belong in the
ingest: a JSON array of Warehouse objects, or later `requirements.txt`
lines. Resolvo then takes the robot module when `--easyconfigs` provides
it. Do not hand-edit the emitted recipe for those names. A PEP 518
`build_system` object with `build-backend = mesonpy` is the mesonpy hint:
listed `requires` become build deps in the Boolean satisfiability (SAT) solve, and the emitter writes
`wrap_mode=default` plus the shared cargo-on-EESSI isolation prelude
(host wrappers off, `LINKER=${CC:-gcc}`, compat `ld` from `uname -m`).
Hatchling stays a `Python-bundle-PyPI` module when the robot provides
it. See [site Python extras](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../howto/pypi-extend.html.md).

## `package bump`

```bash
eb-stack package bump \
  --source RECIPE.eb \
  --toolchain foss/2024a \
  [--version VERSION] \
  [--source-checksum DIGEST] \
  [--dep NAME=VERSION]... \
  --easyconfigs UPSTREAM \
  [--easyconfigs OVERLAY]... \
  [--hierarchy-fixture HIERARCHY.json] \
  [--stack-policy STACK.toml] \
  [--package-config PACKAGE.toml]... \
  [--strict-patches] \
  [--emit-easyblock] \
  [--fetch-checksums] \
  --out-dir BUNDLE
```

A bump writes the same manifest, planned SBOM, profile lock, and recipe layout
as a new package. `--dep` becomes a locked Resolvo override. The solve fails
when that name is not in the robot tree. A name the recipe does not depend on
stays out of the emitted dependency list, and the lock records the pin outcome.
Without `--stack-policy`, the solver uses an unconstrained policy for the
requested toolchain. A changed package version without `--source-checksum`
clears the old digest and produces a visible residual, because source bytes
cannot be inferred safely. `--package-config` is repeatable and applies after
the source recipe is parsed, as it does for `package plan`. `--strict-patches`
fails the bump when a patch's fate across a version change cannot be decided
from the tree; without it the patch is carried and a `patch-decision` residual
records the review flag. `--emit-easyblock` is the same flag as on `package plan`.
`--fetch-checksums` downloads each `sources` entry from the recipe's
`source_urls` when the version changed and `--source-checksum` was omitted,
and writes that SHA-256 into the recipe and the SBOM. A git checkout, a
missing URL, or a failed download stays empty. The attempts are
`sources.fetch.json` (one object per source: `filename`, `url`, `sha256`,
`errors`) and a `source:fetch` residual. See
[output formats](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/formats.html.md).

# Bundle layout

```text
BUNDLE/
  package.plan.json
  package.sbom.cdx.json
  closure.plan.json
  closure.sbom.cdx.json
  build-order.json
  locks/<profile>.lock.json
  easyconfigs/<letter>/<name>/<recipe>.eb
```

`package plan` writes the three closure files whenever `--easyconfigs` is
passed. `package inspect` writes only the plan and planned SBOM.

`package plan` and `package bump` establish the **resolves** claim only when all
requested locks and recipes are written successfully.

See [package bundle reference](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/package-bundles.html.md) for the complete
manifest, planned SBOM, profile-lock, residual, and recipe contract.

# Recipe commands

```bash
eb-stack recipe easyblock NAME
eb-stack recipe easyblock -- -NAME
eb-stack recipe easyblock --charmap

eb-stack recipe templates --export
eb-stack recipe templates --name NAME --version VERSION

eb-stack recipe hierarchy
eb-stack recipe hierarchy --export

eb-stack recipe check \
  --recipe RECIPE.eb \
  --easyconfigs UPSTREAM \
  [--easyconfigs OVERLAY]... \
  [--easyblocks DIR_OR_FILE]... \
  [--require-configopt FLAG]... \
  [--metadata-only] \
  [--verify-sources \
     [--seeded-from ECOSYSTEM \
        [--seeded-source-url URL] \
        [--seeded-git GIT_REMOTE]] \
     [--source-tree DIR]] \
  [--strict]

eb-stack recipe lint RECIPE.eb [RECIPE.eb ...] [--base BEFORE.eb]
eb-stack recipe format RECIPE.eb [RECIPE.eb ...] [--dry-run]
eb-stack recipe format RECIPE.eb --out FORMATTED.eb
```

`recipe easyblock` prints the class EasyBuild derives from a software name
(`EB_` plus the framework character map). `--charmap` prints that map as JSON
instead. A hyphen-leading name is a name, not an option: pass it directly or
after `--`.

`recipe templates --export` prints the constant table and the derived-key
rules. With `--name` and `--version` it prints the values those rules produce
for that pair, using the lowercased name for the forge-account defaults and
`system` for the toolchain. `recipe hierarchy` prints the known fixture
generations as JSON, parent and members, most minimal subtoolchain first.
`--export` prints the whole table: those generations plus the synthetic
GCC-family rule.

`recipe lint` prints JSON with `clean`, `style` (each finding carries
`path`, `line`, `column`, `code`, `severity`, `message`, and, when set,
`info` and `in_review`), `check_contrib`,
and `maintainer_acceptability`. It does not rely on `eb --check-contrib`.
Style codes: E999 (not valid Python; the syntax-tree rules are skipped); the
easyconfigs CI lint F541 (f-string with no placeholder), W605 (invalid escape
sequence), and W291 (trailing whitespace, including inside `description`);
the check-contrib pycodestyle codes E501 (longer than 120) and
E225/E226/E227/E228/E231; the easyconfigs test-suite checks
`EB_PY_NO_USER_SITE`, `EB_SANITY_PATHS_SHAPE`, `EB_LOCAL_VAR_NAMING`,
`EB_REDEFINED_PARAM`, and `EB_CHECKSUM_COUNT`; and the review conventions
`EB_FMT_MISSING_F`, `EB_FSTRING_QUOTE_REUSE`, `EB_TEMPLATE_UNKNOWN` (errors)
and `EB_FMT_PERCENT`, `EB_FMT_CONCAT`, `EB_FMT_TEMPLATE_VAR`,
`EB_SHLIB_HARDCODED`, and `EB_DEP_DUPLICATE` (warnings).
`clean` is false while any error or any in-scope `EB_FMT_*` finding
remains; `error_free` counts errors only. An `EB_FMT_*` finding with
`info` true is outside the review scope (an untouched `%%(...)s`-escaped
entry or, with `--base`, a line unchanged from the base) and does not count.
With `--base` the diff-mode rules also run: `EB_SANITY_ENTRY_REMOVED` and
`EB_EASYBLOCK_CHANGED` (errors), `EB_SANITY_PATHS_REMOVED` (warning), and
`EB_FMT_TEMPLATE_REMOVED`. `EB_FSTRING_ESCAPED_TEMPLATE` and
`EB_DEP_EMPTY_VERSION` are errors. With `--base`, the file
before the edit, it also reports `EB_FMT_TEMPLATE_REMOVED` where a template
was replaced by a Python expression. `f'lib/%(name)s.{SHLIB_EXT}'` is correct
and not flagged. When `eb` is on `PATH`, the command also runs
`eb --check-contrib` and merges those findings (`origin` is
`eb --check-contrib`). A missing `eb` is reported in `check_contrib` and does
not by itself fail the command. Error-severity findings do; warnings do not. `recipe format` only wraps mechanical E501 lines; the other codes stay in
`remaining`.

`recipe check` refuses a recipe that is not valid Python. It prints the
structured dependency result and fails when package
metadata, checksum structure, required configuration flags, or robot
dependencies are invalid. Missing dependencies remain explicit work; the
command does not create placeholder recipes.

`--require-configopt` takes the flag as it appears in `configopts`, dashes
included (`--require-configopt --with-tests`). `--strict` lists every
statement that failed to parse and fails when that list is not empty.
`if`, `for`, `import`, and the other control keywords stay unreported:
that is the tolerant skip, not a parse failure.
`--verify-sources` classifies each source URL and, with `--seeded-from`,
rejects a checksum copied from a different artifact class. `--seeded-source-url`
and `--seeded-git` require `--seeded-from`, which itself requires
`--verify-sources`. `--source-tree` compares the version the unpacked tree
declares with the recipe version.

It also prints `easyblock_resolution`: the class the recipe resolves to
(named, or derived from the software name), the file that defines it, its
bases and its `extra_options` keys. A bundle's own `easyblocks/` directory,
beside the `easyconfigs/` tree the recipe sits in, is searched first. Naming
`--easyblocks` roots, such as an easyblocks checkout, asserts that the set is
complete: a software-specific `EB_` class found in none of them fails the
check with the message EasyBuild would stop on.

`recipe format` only performs deterministic physical-line wrapping. Product
configuration, source selection, checksums, patches, and sanity paths remain
authored content.

# Stack commands

```bash
eb-stack stack solve \
  --easyconfigs TREE [--easyconfigs OVERLAY]... \
  (--stack-policy POLICY.json | --toolchain NAME/VERSION \
   [--root NAME]... [--roots-from-build-list LIST]...) \
  [--baseline-easyconfigs TREE] \
  [--baseline-toolchain-version VERSION] \
  [--baseline-easystack EASYSTACK.yml]... [--baseline-commits-from EB_REPO] \
  [--baseline-also-toolchain NAME/VERSION]... \
  [--filter-deps NAME,NAME...] \
  [--lock-out /tmp/stack.lock.json] \
  [--sbom-out /tmp/stack.cdx.json] \
  [--build-list-out /tmp/build.list] [--build-list-excludes-baseline] \
  [--jenkins-build-list-out /tmp/next.list [--jenkins-flags-from /tmp/previous.list]... \
   [--jenkins-gpu-systems gpu-a,gpu-b] [--jenkins-roots-only]] \
  [--stack-diff-out /tmp/stack.diff.md]

eb-stack stack sbom --lock /tmp/stack.lock.json [--out /tmp/stack.cdx.json]

eb-stack stack order \
  --easyconfigs TREE [--easyconfigs OVERLAY]... \
  --root NAME [--root NAME==VERSION]... \
  [--filter-deps NAME,NAME...] \
  [--out /tmp/build-order.txt] \
  [--oldest] \
  [--easystack-out /tmp/order.yml] \
  [--hashes-out /tmp/hashes.txt]

eb-stack stack easystack \
  --lock /tmp/stack.lock.json \
  [--out stack.yml] \
  [--option FILE.eb:OPTION=VALUE]...

eb-stack stack sections \
  tests/jenkins_sections/next.list \
  --from tests/jenkins_sections/previous.list \
  --out /tmp/grouped.list

eb-stack stack from-commit \
  --easystack 20261011-eb-5.4.0-UCX.yml \
  [--easystack OTHER.yml]... \
  [--easybuild-version 5.4.0] \
  [--easyconfigs-repo ~/src/easybuild-easyconfigs] \
  [--easyblocks-repo ~/src/easybuild-easyblocks] \
  [--json]
```

`stack sbom` reads the easyconfigs the lock names. A runtime dependency
that is also selected is a CycloneDX `dependsOn` edge. A builddependency
is the component property `eb_stack:buildDependsOn`. `stack solve --sbom-out`
writes that same document, checksums included. The MCP tool
`eb_stack_sbom` writes it too. An unreadable path contributes no edge.

`stack solve` is the multi-root EasyBuild stack solver. Package-profile stack
preferences use the TOML schema documented with the package workflow; whole
stack solving uses the JSON `Policy` schema. The policy file is
`--stack-policy`, the same flag `package plan` and `package bump` take.

The baseline is either a previous generation (`--baseline-easyconfigs`, by
default the first `--easyconfigs` tree) or what a set of easystacks installs
(`--baseline-easystack`, repeatable). An easystack baseline is every entry
plus the closure its recipes pin, read from the `--easyconfigs` trees and kept
to the policy toolchain's hierarchy. An entry pinned with `from-commit` is read
from that commit of `--baseline-commits-from` when given, and matched by
filename otherwise. Entries that name no recipe are listed on standard error.
`--baseline-also-toolchain` keeps another family's hierarchy in the baseline,
such as `lfoss/2026.1` beside a `foss/2026.1` solve. `--filter-deps` drops each named dependency before the solve, together
with the subtree under it, using EasyBuild's matching: a bare name,
`name`version`, or `name`[low:high]`. `[` and `]` include a limit, the
opposite bracket excludes it, and an empty side is open. The last spec for
a name wins. Pass EESSI-extend's `EASYBUILD_FILTER_DEPS` list when solving
against a European Environment for Scientific Software Installations (EESSI) baseline, or the build list carries modules the compat
layer already provides.
Against an EESSI version's easystacks, `unchanged` in the stack diff means the
software layer already provides that module, and
`--build-list-excludes-baseline` drops those modules (same name, version,
toolchain and versionsuffix) from the build list, leaving what the site layer
builds on top in dependency order.

A Jenkins build list is one easyconfig filename per line with optional `eb`
flags, `#` for comments. `--roots-from-build-list` takes the package name of
every line as a root. `--jenkins-build-list-out` writes the solved build order
in that format; each package keeps the `--hook`, `--hooks`,
`--include-easyblocks` and `--accept-eula-for` flags of its last line in the
`--jenkins-flags-from` lists, while flags tied to the old recipe
(`--from-commit`, `--from-pr`, `--ignore-test-failure`, `--rebuild`) stay
behind. A module whose name or versionsuffix says CUDA gets
`--include-systems` with the `--jenkins-gpu-systems` list.
`--jenkins-roots-only` writes one line per root application and leaves the
dependencies to `eb --robot`. `stack sbom --lock` re-reads the easyconfigs
named in the lock and restores their runtime `dependsOn` edges.

`stack order` sequences the recipes the roots pin. It does not pick one
version per name, so two builds of one name both appear and stdout reports
`multiple builds of NAME`. `--filter-deps` drops each named dependency
before that order is built, together with the subtree under it, using the
same matching as `stack solve`. When the flag is absent the command reads
`EASYBUILD_FILTER_DEPS`. `--oldest` takes the oldest admissible version of
an unpinned requirement. `--easystack-out` writes that build order.
`--hashes-out` writes one `hash  name-version-toolchain` line per module.
`stack easystack` writes the lock, which is sorted by package name, as the
easystack `eb --easystack` consumes. `--option` is
`<file.eb>:<option>=<value>`. `stack sections` regroups a Jenkins list under
the `#### Title ####` headers of a previous list. Commented entries stay
commented. A name no previous section files goes under `--unfiled`, whose
default is `New in this generation`.

`stack order` keeps every build the recipes pin. A name the generation
builds twice stays twice, in an order that respects every dependency.
`stack solve` picks one version of that name; this command does not.
`--root` repeats, and `name==version` pins one build. `--oldest` takes the
oldest admissible version of an unpinned requirement. The default is the
newest. `--out` is one easyconfig path per line (default
`build-order.txt`). `--easystack-out` writes that same sequence as an
easystack. `--hashes-out` writes one line per module, `<sha256>  <module>`,
a digest of the easyconfig and of the hashes of everything it needs. A
module whose recipe could not be read is still listed, and the stdout line
`incomplete`` counts those. Stdout ends with `order`<path> builds=<N>`.
A name with two builds also prints `multiple builds of <name>:`.

`stack easystack` writes `easyconfigs:` as a YAML list of filenames, in
lock order. `--option` repeats. The option is spelled as on the `eb`
command line without its dashes, for example
`--option CUDA-12.8.0.eb:accept-eula-for=CUDA`. A file with options is a
mapping; a file without them is a string. Stdout is
`easystack`<path> entries`<N> of=<packages>`.

`stack sections` reads the build list
and regroups its entries under the `#### Title ####` headers of `--from`.
Each entry keeps its flags and whether it is commented out. Packages no
section of `--from` names go under `--unfiled` (default ~New in this
generation~), last. The comment block before the first entry stays on top.
Stdout is `list`<path> sections`<written> of=<previous+1>`. The `of` count
is the previous list's section count plus the unfiled header.

The recorded lists are `tests/jenkins_sections/previous.list` and
`tests/jenkins_sections/next.list`. The command in the synopsis writes:

```text
# next generation

#### MPI ####
# OpenMPI-5.0.10-GCC-15.2.0.eb --hooks=/sw/h.py

#### Chemistry ####
# GROMACS-2025.0-foss-2025b.eb

#### New in this generation ####
# CP2K-2026.1-foss-2025b.eb
```

`stack from-commit` reads each `--easystack` and reports every `from-commit`
and `include-easyblocks-from-commit` pin. The release is
`--easybuild-version X.Y.Z`, or the `eb-X.Y.Z` in the file name when the
flag is omitted. The flag overrides the file name. The tag is
`easybuild-easyconfigs-vX.Y.Z` in `--easyconfigs-repo`, and
`easybuild-easyblocks-vX.Y.Z` in `--easyblocks-repo`. A pin is `released`
when that commit is an ancestor of the tag (a commit is an ancestor of
itself), `newer` when the commit is in the checkout and is not an ancestor,
or `unknown` when the commit or the tag is missing. `unknown` does not
guess. A `released` `from-commit` pin also says `blob=same` or
`blob=differs`, comparing the easyconfig blob named by the tree at the pin
with the blob at the tag. An `include-easyblocks-from-commit` pin compares
the tree of the pin with the tree of the tag, because that pin does not
name one easyconfig. `released` and `same` can be removed. `released` and
`differs` needs a person: the release is not the pinned file. The command
exits 1 when `released` is not zero. `--json` prints the same report as
JSON. See [from-commit pins already in an EasyBuild release](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../howto/from-commit-released.html.md).

# `pr-overlap`

```bash
eb-stack pr-overlap \
  --pr PR.json [PR.json...] [--pr PR.json]... \
  [--open OWNER/NAME] \
  [--base-ref REF] \
  --easyconfigs TREE [--easyconfigs TREE]... \
  [--commit-tree COMMIT=DIR]... \
  --installed installed.txt \
  [--eessi-version 2026.06] \
  [--installed-label LABEL] \
  [--exclude-path SUBSTR]... \
  [--include-path SUBSTR]... \
  [--filter-deps SPEC,SPEC...] \
  [--installed-modulerc PATH]... \
  [--easyblocks DIR]... \
  [--easyblocks-commit COMMIT=DIR]... \
  [--generated-at RFC3339] \
  [--merge-order] \
  [--merged N]... \
  [--impact N]... \
  [--repo-url URL] \
  [--out-dir /tmp/pr-overlap]
```

Reads each pull request's easystack changes as data. It does not run the
pull request and it does not build. Several JSON paths may follow one
`--pr`, matching what a glob of the per-pull-request files expands to.
For the given `--eessi-version` it keeps
the easystack entries present at head and absent from base, finds those
easyconfigs on the robot path, and closes them against `--installed`.

`--easyconfigs` is the release robot tree. Later trees win on the same
name, version, toolchain, and versionsuffix. `--commit-tree` is the
easyconfigs tree at one `from-commit`, and it wins over the release tree for
entries pinned to that commit.

`--exclude-path` drops easystack paths that contain the substring.
`--include-path`, when given, keeps only paths that contain one of the
substrings. An empty include list keeps every path that survived the
excludes.

An installed module is a leaf. Entries under a `rebuilds/` easystack are
built even when installed. A requirement no easyconfig satisfies is recorded
and the rest of the closure is still written.

`--filter-deps` is comma-separated and uses the same matching as
`stack solve`. A filtered dependency is dropped before the walk, so the
modules reachable only through it are never opened. When the flag is omitted
and `EASYBUILD_FILTER_DEPS` is set, that value is used. A non-empty flag
wins over the environment.

`--installed-modulerc` is a `.modulerc.lua` file or a module tree. A
`module_version("Name/full", "alias")` line makes `Name/alias` installed
when `Name/full` is on the installed list.

`--easyblocks` is the installed `easybuild/easyblocks` package. Passing any
root checks every easyblock class. A software-specific class none of the
roots defines is recorded as `easyblock <class> missing` and that module is
left out of `to_build`. Its dependencies stay. `--easyblocks-commit` is
`<commit>=<dir>` for one `include-easyblocks-from-commit`: the directory is
the easyblock files that commit touches, matching what EasyBuild includes
ahead of the installed package. A class found there is counted, and the
record notes the commit. A commit an entry names whose directory was not
passed is noted as not provided.

`--kind` selects the pull request shape. `software-layer` is the default
and reads easystack additions. `easyconfigs` reads changed `.eb` files.
`--installed` is required for `software-layer`. For `easyconfigs` it is
optional: with the flag, `to_build` starts as the closure minus that list;
without it, `to_build` starts as the modules the base tree does not provide.
A modified easyconfig, and a base-tree module classed `must-rebuild`, then
join `to_build`, including when the module is already installed. `review`
and `no-rebuild` reverse dependents are listed on the record and left out
of `to_build`. A bundle whose `exts_list` names the patched package is
`must-rebuild`. A runtime dependency is `no-rebuild`. A dependent reached
only through builddependencies is `review`.

`--eessi-version` is ignored for `easyconfigs` and is omitted from the
record. `--repo-url` defaults to
`https://github.com/EESSI/software-layer` for `software-layer` and to
`https://github.com/easybuilders/easybuild-easyconfigs` for `easyconfigs`.

`--open OWNER/NAME` reads the open pull requests of that repository over
HTTPS and adds them to any `--pr` files. It requires `--kind easyconfigs`.
The repository has to be `owner/name`. `--base-ref` is the git ref for the
base text of each changed file and defaults to `develop`. A name such as
`release/2026.1` is accepted. A repository or ref that fails those checks
is an error before a request is sent and before the output directory is
written. A failure of the request itself is reported after the request is
sent and still writes nothing.

This easyconfigs command was run on the recorded open pull requests. It
wrote 4 records and exited 0. The summary line was
`prs`4 records`4 shared_modules`1 skipped_easyconfigs`0`.

```bash
eb-stack pr-overlap \
  --kind easyconfigs \
  --pr tests/pr_overlap_easyconfigs_open/prs.json \
  --easyconfigs tests/pr_overlap_easyconfigs_open/tree \
  --generated-at 2026-10-24T00:00:00Z \
  --repo-url https://github.com/easybuilders/easybuild-easyconfigs \
  --out-dir /tmp/ec-overlap
```

The JSON is the four open pull requests recorded under
`tests/pr_overlap_easyconfigs_open/`. 22823 and 24575 share
`Mathematica/14.2.1`.

The output directory contains `prs/<N>.toml`, `overlap.toml`, and `overlap.md`.
See [output formats](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/formats.html.md) for the records. A closed pull
request's file is removed: the directory is the open set of this run.

`--repo-url` defaults to `https://github.com/EESSI/software-layer`. The
report links each pull request there. Pass another URL to link somewhere
else, or an empty URL to write `#N` text.

`--merge-order` also writes `merge-order.toml` and appends a Merge order
table to `overlap.md`. Without the flag, `prs/`, `overlap.toml`, and
`overlap.md` are unchanged. `--merged N` repeats and implies
`--merge-order`. N has to be a number in the `--pr` input that
produced a record. This run names a missing one:

```bash
eb-stack pr-overlap --pr tests/pr_overlap_layer/prs.json \
  --easyconfigs tests/pr_overlap_layer \
  --installed tests/pr_overlap_layer/installed.txt \
  --installed-label none \
  --generated-at 2026-10-24T00:00:00Z \
  --merge-order --merged 1585 --merged 999 \
  --out-dir /tmp/pr-overlap-out
```

The error is `--merged 999: no pull request with that number`. A number
that is in the input but changes no easyconfig and no easystack is
`--merged N: pull request N has no record (no easyconfigs or easystack change)`.
A rejected
`--merged` or `--impact` does not create the output directory and does not
change files already in it. The same
command with only `--merged 1585` treats pull request 1585 as already
installed and orders the rest. Pull request 1585 adds
`SciPy-bundle-2026.05-gfbf-2026.1.eb` and pull request 1728 adds
`PLUMED-2.10.0-foss-2026.1.eb`. Both change
`easystacks/software.eessi.io/2026.06/eessi-2026.06-eb-5.4.0-2026.1.yml`.

`--impact N` writes `merge-impact.toml`. Repeat the flag. N has to be a
number in the `--pr` input that produced a record. A number that is not
in the input is `--impact 999: no pull request with that number`. A pull
request that is in the input but has no record is
`--impact N: pull request N has no record (no easyconfigs or easystack change)`.
The file is the effect
of merging that pull request alone: other pull requests whose `to_build`
shrinks, and depends-on edges from it that resolve. It is not the residual
after earlier steps of `--merge-order`, and it does not write
`merge-order.toml` unless that flag (or `--merged`) is also set. A number
that is also passed to `--merged` is an error:
`--impact N: already listed in --merged`. Modules those merged pull
requests build are already installed, so they do not appear in `shrinks`
and those pull requests are not listed under `affected`. For
`--kind easyconfigs`, `resolves` lists the modules on a `depends-on`
row from that pull request, and `after` in `merge-order.toml` lists the
pull request that adds them or that patches a module this pull request
builds a dependent of. The recorded easyconfigs run is
[close open easybuild-easyconfigs pull requests](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../howto/easyconfigs-pr-overlap.html.md).

# `rebuild-set`

```bash
eb-stack rebuild-set \
  --changed FILE.eb [--changed FILE.eb]... \
  --easystack STACK.yml [--easystack STACK.yml]... \
  --easyconfigs TREE [--easyconfigs TREE]... \
  [--commit-tree COMMIT=DIR]... \
  --installed installed.txt \
  [--installed-label LABEL] \
  [--filter-deps SPEC,SPEC...] \
  [--installed-modulerc PATH]... \
  [--easyblocks DIR]... \
  [--easyblocks-commit COMMIT=DIR]... \
  [--generated-at RFC3339] \
  [--prefix "$EESSI_SOFTWARE_PATH"] \
  [--check-static] \
  [--out-dir /tmp/rebuild-set]
```

Resolves the deployed easystacks and the installed reverse dependents of
each patched easyconfig. The patch keeps the filename and the version.
Classification starts from the easyconfig graph. The closure stays inside
the patched module's toolchain generation: an unpinned dependency is
resolved in the dependent's own generation, and a module from another
generation is not a row.

`--changed` is an easyconfig filename. Repeat it, or pass a file that does
not end in `.eb`: one filename per line, blank lines and `#` comments
skipped. The basename is what is matched. A filename that is not in the
deployed graph is listed under `missing` and has no row.

`--easystack` is a deployed easystack, repeated. Every entry is a root.
`--easyconfigs`, `--commit-tree`, `--installed`, `--filter-deps`,
`--installed-modulerc`, `--easyblocks`, and `--easyblocks-commit` mean the
same as for `pr-overlap`. `--filter-deps` drops dependency tuples and does
not strip `exts_list`. A missing easyblock class is recorded and the
module stays, because it is already installed.

A runtime dependency is `no-rebuild`. A dependent reached only through
builddependencies is `review`. The patched easyconfig, and a bundle whose
`exts_list` names that package and version, are `must-rebuild`. A toolchain
edge is not classified. A review dependent is one row, and `changed` lists
every patched easyconfig that put it there. See
[what an in-place patch forces a rebuild of](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../explanation/rebuild-set.html.md).

`--prefix` reads `software/<name>/<version>/lib**/**.a`. No static archive
makes a builddependency-only dependent no-rebuild, with the reason ~no
static archive installed~. Archives that are installed keep the row in
review and are named. A missing install directory is a note.

`--check-static` needs `--prefix`. It compares defined dynamic symbols of
the remaining review dependents with the patched library's exports. A hit
is must-rebuild. No hit is no-rebuild. An empty export set stays in
review. The scan sees dynamic symbols only, so a hidden or inlined static
link is a false no-rebuild, and a short name shared with another library
is a false must-rebuild.

The output directory contains `rebuild-set.json`, `rebuild-set.md`, and
`rebuilds/<YYYYMMDD>-eb-<version>-cve-patches.yml`. The easystack contains
class `must-rebuild` only, including a dependent that `--check-static`
promoted. A second run replaces the `rebuilds/*.yml` files.

# `component-reach`

```bash
eb-stack component-reach \
  (--component NAME --version VER | --purl PKG:TYPE/NAME@VER | --cve CVE-ID) \
  --generation 2026.1 \
  --easyconfigs TREE [--easyconfigs TREE]... \
  [--installed installed.txt] \
  [--easystack STACK.yml]... \
  [--easystack-url https://.../STACK.yml]... \
  [--compat-layer FILE] \
  [--filter-deps SPEC,SPEC...] \
  [--generated-at RFC3339] \
  [--out-dir /tmp/component-reach]
```

Lists every easyconfig and installed module in one toolchain generation
that carries a component, then feeds the recipes that contain it into
the rebuild closure. See
[which modules carry a component](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../howto/component-reach.html.md).

Pass `--component` and `--version`, or `--purl`, or `--cve`. `--version`
is an exact version, `*`, or a requirement such as `>=8,<9`. With
`--purl` it replaces the version in the URL. The purl type selects the
carriers. `generic` and `github` match the easyconfig name. `pypi`,
`cargo`, `npm`, `golang`, and `cran` match an extension or a bundled
component of that language, plus a crate for `cargo` and a wheel for
`pypi`. Another type exits 2: the error says that purl type has no
carrier model. `pkg:cargo/curl` does not match the cURL recipe.
`--cve` resolves the id through Open Source Vulnerabilities (OSV), follows GitHub Security Advisory (GHSA), RUSTSEC, PYSEC, and
GO aliases when the Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) record has only a git range, and keeps named
version tags such as `libXpm-3.5.17`. A range that is not SEMVER or
ECOSYSTEM, or an event that does not parse, is reported under
Unresolved ranges. A package whose ranges were all unparsed counts as
review. Several affected packages are written as one document with
`kind` `cve`. The summary line includes `changed`, `must-rebuild`,
`review`, and `no-rebuild`.

Names match ignoring ASCII letter case, on a whole token. A recipe is in the
generation when its toolchain version equals `--generation`, or when the
toolchain is a non-system member of the known foss hierarchy for that
generation.

A hit is a dependency or builddependency tuple, a bundle `components`
entry, an `exts_list` extension, a Cargo crate (a `crates` tuple, a
filename such as `libz-sys-1.1.29.tar.gz`, or a checksum key such as
`rustls-webpki-0.102.8.tar.gz`), a Python wheel (`.whl` in `sources`,
`checksums`, an `exts_list` source, or `source_tmpl`), or a versioned
name in `sources` or `patches`. A `+name-version` fragment inside a crate
version counts as that vendored version. The recipe's own tarball is not
a crate it carries. A dependency or builddependency is a carrier and
is not a patched root. The other roles are: the recipe contains the
component, and its filename is a changed input of the closure.

`--easystack-url` repeats and must be `https://`. It is read the same
way as `--easystack`.

`--compat-layer` is `name version` or `name==version` per line, `#`
comments skipped. The compat layer is not an easyconfig, so a hit has an
empty easyconfig and a note, and it is not a closure edge.
`--filter-deps` matches `rebuild-set` and reads `EASYBUILD_FILTER_DEPS`
when the flag is omitted. It does not strip `exts_list`.

With no `--easystack`, every easyconfig in the generation is the stack.
With no `--installed`, every module in the generation is treated as
installed. Pass both to visit only a mounted prefix. The closure classes
are the same as `rebuild-set`, and they stay inside the generation.

The output directory contains `component-reach.toml`, `component-reach.json`,
and `component-reach.md`. The TOML file starts with
`# Generated by `eb-stack component-reach`.`

# Target commands

```bash
eb-stack target list \
  --config examples/targets/base.toml \
  --config examples/targets/site.example.toml
eb-stack target doctor \
  --config examples/targets/base.toml \
  --config examples/targets/site.example.toml \
  --target NAME
```

Target layers are applied in argument order. A complete target contains:

- transport: local or SSH;
- executor: direct or Slurm;
- runtime: host, Podman, or Docker;
- EasyBuild workload: command, robot paths, work root, temporary root, and
  environment.

`target doctor` probes each layer separately and reports the exact routed
command, exit code, stdout, and stderr.

See [build target configuration](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/targets.html.md) for complete layer schemas,
replacement semantics, ABI isolation, and the runnable local Podman target.

# Campaign commands

```bash
eb-stack campaign run \
  --bundle BUNDLE \
  --config examples/targets/base.toml \
  --config examples/targets/site.example.toml \
  --target NAME \
  --state /tmp/campaign.json

eb-stack campaign status --state /tmp/campaign.json

eb-stack campaign finding claim \
  --state /tmp/campaign.json --id FINDING --owner WORKER

eb-stack campaign finding resolve \
  --state /tmp/campaign.json --id FINDING --owner WORKER \
  --action TEXT --evidence TEXT [--change PATH]...
```

`campaign run` resumes state with matching package identity, increments the
attempt, stages the bundle, runs every emitted recipe, and executes each
profile's verification commands. Transport, executor, runtime, interrupted,
checksum, patch, dependency, configure, compile, link, test, install, sanity,
resource, timeout, and unknown failures are persisted as typed findings.

Finding claims are exclusive. A resolution records an action, evidence, and
changed paths. A successful retry supersedes matching open or in-progress
findings. Campaign state reports `resolves`, `builds`, and `binary_verified`
independently.

See [campaign state and typed findings](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/campaigns.html.md) for the serialized
state, claim ladder, class/disposition table, and repair protocol.

# `repro summary`

```bash
eb-stack repro summary \
  --scores DIR \
  [--ratchet ratchet.json] \
  [--json]
```

Reads every `*.json` case score the reproduction suite wrote under
`--scores` (the directory `EB_REPRO_SCORES` points at when the suite runs)
and prints the scoreboard table:

```text
| Case | PR | Score | Allowance | Residual |
|---+---+---+---+---|
| reproduces_gromacs | - | EXACT | 1 | 0 |

2 cases: 1 EXACT, 1 SEMANTIC, 0 MATERIAL; allowance total 1
```

`Score` is `EXACT`, `SEMANTIC`, or `MATERIAL`. `Allowance` is how many
hand-added lines the case still forgives. `Residual` is the raw diff lines
left after that allowance. A pull request number prints as `#N`; a case
with none prints `-`. `--json` prints the case records instead of the
table: `case`, `pull_request`, `source`, `target`, `score`, `allowance`,
`stale_allowance`, `residual_lines`. `--ratchet` reads
`{"note", "cases", "total"}`. `--ratchet` exits nonzero when a case's
allowance disagrees with the committed count, when a case is missing from
the file, or when `total` is not the sum of `cases`. A matching run also prints
`ratchet: <N> cases hold at <total>`. An empty `--scores` directory is an
error. See [reproduction fidelity](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../explanation/fidelity.html.md).

# `easyblock-reach`

```bash
eb-stack easyblock-reach \
  --easyblocks EASYBLOCKS \
  [--framework FRAMEWORK]... \
  --easyconfigs EASYCONFIGS \
  [--file PATH]... \
  [--range A..B | --pr N] \
  [--remote origin] [--base develop] [--repo CLONE] \
  [--installed MODULES.txt] [--reverse] \
  [--generated-at RFC3339] \
  [--out-dir /tmp/easyblock-reach]
```

Pass at least one of `--file`, `--range`, and `--pr`, and at least one of
`--easyblocks` and `--framework`. `--range` and `--pr` read Python files
from the clone (`--repo`, or the first `--easyblocks` path). The report is
`reach.toml`, `reach.json`, and `reach.md`. See
[which easyconfigs an easyblock change reaches](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../howto/easyblock-reach.html.md).

# MCP

```bash
eb-stack mcp [--workspace ROOT]
```

`--workspace` sets `EB_STACK_WORKSPACE` for the recipe file tools. When it is
omitted, an existing `EB_STACK_WORKSPACE` is kept, and otherwise the server's
current directory is the root.
